question: Who prepares the weekly statement of charges for deviation, and by when must it be issued?
expected_answer: The RLDC sends the deviation data for the previous week (ending Sunday midnight) to the RPC Secretariat by Thursday; the RPC Secretariat issues the statement of charges to all regional entities by the following Tuesday.

question: What is a 'Renewable Super Rich State' under the DSM Regulations?
expected_answer: A State whose combined installed capacity of solar and wind generating stations under its control area is 5,000 MW or more.

question: How are deviation charges settled for start-up power drawn before the COD of a generating unit?
expected_answer: Payable at the reference charge rate or the contract rate; if neither exists, at the weighted average ACP of the Day Ahead Market segments of all power exchanges for that time block. The same applies to power drawn to run auxiliaries during shutdown.
key_facts: payable at RR or contract rate
else weighted average ACP of DAM of all power exchanges

question: What must a regional entity do if it paid its deviation charges late at any time in the previous financial year?
expected_answer: Open a Letter of Credit of 110% of its average payable weekly deviation liability of the previous financial year, in favour of the RLDC, within a fortnight from the start of the current financial year. If it later fails to pay into the Pool Account on time, the RLDC may encash the LC, and the entity must recoup it within 3 days.
key_facts: within a fortnight of start of FY

question: How are deviation charges applied when a seller suffers a forced outage?
expected_answer: Notwithstanding clauses (1) to (11), charges for deviation are at the reference charge rate for at most eight time blocks or until its schedule is revised, whichever is earlier.
key_facts: or until schedule revision, whichever earlier

question: What does the Deviation and Ancillary Service Pool Account receive credit for?
expected_answer: Payments of charges for deviation (Reg 8) and late payment surcharge (Reg 10); payments by SRAS providers for SRAS-Down and by TRAS providers for TRAS-Down despatched under the Ancillary Services Regulations; and other charges notified by the Commission.
key_facts: deviation charges and late payment surcharge
notes: DSM 2024 Reg 9(5). Dev R10 asked who maintains the account; this asks what it receives

question: What are the deviation volume limits for a solar seller today?
expected_answer: From 01.04.2026: VLwS(1) = deviation up to 5% DWS; VLwS(2) = beyond 5% and up to 10% DWS. (Over-injection: contract rate / 90% / zero beyond VLwS(2); under-injection: contract rate / 110% / 200% beyond VLwS(2).) Newer projects covered by Reg 8(4A) are treated at par with general sellers instead.
notes: DSM 2024 Reg 8(4) Note-1(ii). As of the run date

question: What are the deviation volume limits for a buyer that is an RE-rich State?
expected_answer: VLB(1) = deviation up to 200 MW; VLB(2) = beyond 200 MW and up to 300 MW; VLB(3) = beyond 300 MW.

question: What is paid for infirm power injected by a thermal generating unit before its trial run is complete?
expected_answer: From first synchronisation until successful completion of the trial run, it is paid at the Normal Rate of Charges for Deviation for each time block, with a ceiling of ₹2.86/kWh (Second Amendment, from 01.07.2025). When f > 50.05 Hz, the charge is zero.
key_facts: Normal Rate for each time block
notes: DSM Second Amendment 2025, Reg 8(8)(2) and (4). Dev R08 / 4c A2-A3 covered standalone ESS, not thermal

question: What does a general seller receive or pay for over-injection beyond 10% DGS or 100 MW when frequency is 50.10 Hz or higher?
expected_answer: It receives nothing (zero below 50.10 Hz) and, at f ≥ 50.10 Hz, it pays 10% of RR.
key_facts: pays 10% of RR at f ≥ 50.10 Hz

question: On 01.06.2024, within how many days did a regional entity have to pay its deviation charges?
expected_answer: 7 days from issue of the statement of charges by the RPC (DSM Regulations, 2022, Reg 10(1)), with late payment surcharge of 0.04% per day of delay. The 10-day period applies only from 16.09.2024 (DSM 2024).

question: On 15.03.2026, what were the deviation volume limits for a wind seller?
expected_answer: VLwS(1) = deviation up to 15% DWS; VLwS(2) = beyond 15% and up to 20% DWS (limits for the period up to 31.03.2026).
notes: DSM 2024 Reg 8(4) Note-1(i). Must not give the 10%/15% limits from 01.04.2026

question: As of 01.11.2024, how was the 'Available Capacity' of a wind or solar seller defined?
expected_answer: The cumulative capacity rating of the wind turbines or solar inverters capable of generating power in a given time block. The limit 'to the quantum of connectivity granted' was added only from 23.12.2024 by the First Amendment.
key_facts: cumulative capacity rating of turbines or inverters
capable of generating in the time block
no connectivity limit on that date
notes: DSM 2024 Reg 3(1)(g); First Amendment para 2.1 is not in force on the date

question: On 20.06.2025, what was paid for infirm power injected by a thermal unit before completing its trial run?
expected_answer: Nothing: the charges for injection of infirm power were zero (Reg 8(8) as substituted by the First Amendment). Payment at the Normal Rate capped at ₹2.86/kWh started only on 01.07.2025.
key_facts: Normal Rate with ₹2.86 cap only from 01.07.2025
notes: Pairs with E09 (same question, later date)

question: Did the final Third Amendment adopt the draft's proposal on the deadline for paying deviation charges?
expected_answer: Not as drafted. The draft (26.05.2026) proposed replacing the 10-day deadline with the timeline in the Detailed Procedure for the National Deviation and Ancillary Services Pool Account. The final Third Amendment (in force 31.08.2026) keeps the 10 days and adds 'or within such timeline as stipulated in the Detailed Procedure' as an alternative. Draft content must be labelled as a draft.
key_facts: adds Detailed Procedure timeline as alternative
notes: Also closes OB-2 (the amendment did NOT replace the 10-day rule)

question: A run-of-river hydro station is scheduled at 200 MW and injects 240 MW in a 15-minute block on 15.09.2026. Its reference charge rate is ₹3.50/kWh. What is the deviation charge?
expected_answer: ₹26,250.00 receivable by the seller. Deviation +40 MW (20% DGS); limit = 15% DGS or 150 MW, whichever is less = 30 MW. 30 MW × 0.25 h = 7.5 MWh at RR (₹3.50) = ₹26,250; the remaining 10 MW (2.5 MWh) at zero.

question: On 10.06.2027, a wind plant commissioned in 2020 with 100 MW available capacity is scheduled at 60 MW and injects 45 MW in a block. Its contract rate is ₹3.00/kWh. What is the deviation charge?
expected_answer: ₹11,842.50 payable. X = 95% (FY 2027-28, wind; from the secondary summary of CERC's order — must be said). Denominator = 0.95 × 100 + 0.05 × 60 = 98 MW; deviation −15 MW = 15.31% DWS. 9.8 MW (2.45 MWh) at ₹3.00 = ₹7,350; 4.9 MW (1.225 MWh) at 110% = ₹4,042.50; 0.3 MW (0.075 MWh) at 200% = ₹450.
notes: FR-10 check: X comes from the secondary source. Commissioned 2020, so Reg 8(4A) does not apply

question: An RE-rich State scheduled to draw 1,000 MW actually draws 1,250 MW in a block on 01.10.2026, when the frequency is 49.95 Hz. The Normal Rate is ₹5.00/kWh. What is its deviation charge?
What deviation charges apply to solar generators under the Tamil Nadu (TNERC) regulations?
expected_answer: Not found in the documents (state regulations are not in the corpus; CR-2 Batch B not approved).
notes: FR-6. Different state from the 4c A5 check (Karnataka)

question: What was the Area Clearing Price on the Indian Energy Exchange yesterday?
expected_answer: Not found in the documents (live market prices are not in the regulations).

question: How long is a time block used for deviation settlement?
expected_answer: 15 minutes. The DSM Regulations define 'time block' as defined in the Grid Code; the Grid Code defines it as the block (duration specified by the Commission) for which energy meters record values, starting at 00.00 hours, presently 15 minutes.
notes: Cross-document: DSM refers to the Grid Code

question: How much notice must an SRAS provider give before modifying or withdrawing its standing consent?
expected_answer: At least 48 hours, except in case of forced outage.

question: What is the minimum installed capacity for a generating station to apply for connectivity to the ISTS?
expected_answer: 50 MW, either individually or as an aggregate of 50 MW and above through a Lead Generator or Lead ESS. (The Third Amendment adds a separate route for 5–50 MW projects connecting to the BBMB network.)
key_facts: individually or aggregate through lead generator/ESS

question: What is 'market coupling' under the Power Market Regulations?
expected_answer: The process in which bids collected from all power exchanges are matched, considering all bid types, to discover a uniform market clearing price for the Day Ahead Market, Real-Time Market or another notified market, subject to market splitting.
key_facts: bids from all power exchanges matched

question: Can a wind or solar seller revise its schedule because of a forecasting error if it sold the power in a collective transaction?
expected_answer: No. A WS seller may revise its schedule for forecasting error only for bilateral transactions, not collective transactions; the revision takes effect as per Reg 49(4)(c).
notes: IEGC 2023 Reg 49(8). Not changed by the IEGC First Amendment
